observations.text: SP flew the echelon turn as No2 at the level expected for this Training Section, holding the wingline with continuous IP direction on bank and power. Lateral separation was kept close to the 10 foot reference, but IP calls were needed on each roll-in to stop the build-up before one and a half wing spans, and the vertical position drifted below the midpoint of the leader's wing whenever bank passed 45 degrees. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent recognition of the vertical and lateral references is expected to improve.

SP completed the echelon turn as No2 with the IP's verbal prompts only, with no control input required from the front cockpit. Lateral separation stayed inside one and a half wing spans and never exceeded the 10 foot reference by more than 50 feet, and the A/C was flown in a solid way through the pre-planned turns up to 60 degrees of bank. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained the Echelon position as No2 through the pre-planned turns, with only minor deviations. Lateral separation exceeded the 10 foot reference by no more than 25 feet and vertical position stayed within 6 feet of the midpoint of the leader's wing, every deviation being recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP held the Echelon position as No2 accurately and promptly throughout the pre-planned turns up to 60 degrees of bank. Lateral separation remained between 10 and 20 feet, vertical position within 4 feet of the midpoint of the leader's wing, and longitudinal position within 4 feet of the references set by the leading edge of the wing and the trailing edge of the stabilator. Corrections were smooth, solid and applied in time, with no IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the echelon turn as No2 with exceptional precision, holding the wingline references with negligible deviations in all three axes. Lateral, vertical and longitudinal separation showed no perceptible departure from the briefed 10 foot reference and from the midpoint of the leader's wing, even through the 60 degree bank turns. Control inputs were smooth and anticipatory, above the levels desired for this Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to late and insufficient power reduction as No1 rolled into the turn, did not hold the briefed longitudinal reference and moved forward of the leading edge of the leader's wing, with the result of a longitudinal deviation of about 15 feet. The IP had to direct the correction and fly part of the repositioning back to the Echelon position.

SP, due to a perceptual error in judging closure and lateral separation, did not keep the safe distance of approximately 10 feet and closed inside the reference during the roll-in. The IP intervened on the controls to open the lateral separation, with the result that the maneuver was not completed without assistance.

SP flew the echelon turn as No2 to the level required for this Training Section, completing it after the IP's verbal prompts on bank and lineup. Lateral separation opened to one and a half wing spans, some 50 feet beyond the 10 foot reference, before the correction was applied, and the vertical position was returned to the midpoint of the leader's wing only after a delayed recognition. Marginal performance for the Training Section - timely recognition of the wingline references without prompting is expected to improve.

SP maintained the Echelon position as No2 through the pre-planned turns up to 60 degrees of bank, with only minor deviations. Lateral separation exceeded the 10 foot reference by about 25 feet at the roll-in and vertical position stayed within 6 feet of the wing midpoint, all deviations being recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP held the Echelon position as No2 with accuracy and speed, controlling the A/C in a smooth and solid way throughout the maneuver. Lateral separation was contained between 10 and 20 feet, while vertical and longitudinal deviations did not exceed 4 feet from the midpoint of the leader's wing and from the briefed fore and aft references. No IP prompting or intervention was required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the echelon turn as No2 to a standard well above that desired for this Training Section, with negligible deviations in lateral, vertical and longitudinal separation. Position on the wingline was anticipated rather than chased, and the 10 foot reference and the wing midpoint were held without perceptible excursion through 60 degrees of bank. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a cross-check limited to the leader's fuselage instead of the wingtip and canopy rail references, did not fly the vertical position at the midpoint of the leader's wing and drifted low as bank increased, with the result of a vertical deviation of more than 15 feet. The IP directed the correction and flew part of the repositioning to the Echelon position, so the turn was not completed without assistance.

SP, due to an inadequate anti-G straining manoeuvre for the G applied in the 60 degree bank turn, did not control the A/C in a smooth and solid way and lost the wingline references. Lateral separation opened well beyond one and a half wing spans, more than 50 feet outside the 10 foot reference, with the result that the IP took the A/C to re-establish the Echelon position.

SP, due to over-controlling in roll while chasing the leader's bank instead of stabilizing on the wingline references, did not make the appropriate corrections in time. Lateral separation reached one and a half wing spans, about 50 feet beyond the 10 foot reference, and the position was re-established only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the deviation recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to distraction by intra-flight radio traffic at the roll-in, did not hold the vertical position at the midpoint of the leader's wing and allowed the A/C to settle low. The vertical deviation reached 10 feet and was recognized only after the IP's verbal prompt, with the result that the correction back to the Echelon position was applied late.

SP maintained the Echelon position as No2 within the desired standards through the pre-planned turns up to 60 degrees of bank; however, lateral separation twice built to about 25 feet beyond the 10 foot reference before being corrected. All deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - smoother power control at the roll-in and steadier use of the wingtip reference are expected to improve.

SP held the Echelon position as No2 accurately and promptly, without IP prompting or intervention. Lateral separation stayed between 10 and 20 feet, vertical position within 4 feet of the midpoint of the leader's wing, and longitudinal position within 4 feet of the references at the leading edge of the wing and the trailing edge of the stabilator. Control of the A/C was smooth and solid throughout the pre-planned turns. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the echelon turn as No2 with exceptional precision, holding the briefed 10 foot lateral reference and the wing midpoint with negligible deviations through turns up to 60 degrees of bank. Corrections were anticipatory and so small as to be barely perceptible, and the formation position was never in question. Performance was above the levels desired for this Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.
